# CANDIDATE: NAMED_LEVEL_VOLUME_CLIMAX_FADE

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

At significant named levels (prior day high or prior day low), a volume-climax bar with a long wick rejecting the level often signals exhaustion and a mean-reverting move. This pattern captures liquidity exhaustion where aggressive volume fails to sustain a breakout, leading to a reversal. The edge exists because named levels act as psychological barriers where stop-losses and option barriers cluster, and volume climaxes indicate last-gasp attempts to breach the level before reversal.

## Mechanism

Entry: Identify when SPY touches prior day high (resistance) or prior day low (support) within 0.1% tolerance on a 5-minute bar. If the touching bar has volume > 2× the 20-bar average volume (volume climax) AND wick-to-body ratio > 2 (long wick opposite the level direction: upper wick for resistance touch, lower wick for support touch) AND closes within the opposite half of the bar's range (close below midpoint for resistance touch, above midpoint for support touch), enter a fade position: short at resistance touch, long at support touch. Exit: Initial stop placed beyond the extreme of the climax bar (above its high for shorts, below its low for longs). Target: 1× ATR(14) from entry price OR the next opposing named level (prior day low for shorts, prior day high for longs), whichever is closer. Regime filter: Only active between 10:00-12:00 ET; disabled first 20 minutes after open and during high-impact news (FOMC, CPI, NFP) when named levels are frequently swept.
